correctness.rationale: In a period bin of width eta, if two chosen periodic representatives were not separated for times from 0 to T, the piecewise-linear reparameterization matching their periods changes the time argument by at most eta on each fundamental period. The only small-time displacement term is evaluated on the periodic orbit of the second representative, so the periodic-point modulus alone makes the reparameterized orbits remain inside a geometric-separation constant; distinct periodic orbits are therefore separated. A compact set meeting every regular orbit supplies representatives, and summing separated-set bounds over O(T) period bins gives the claimed exponential upper bound. In the strictness example, the added real translation component is topologically compatible, has one nonperiodic orbit, makes global uniform small-time continuity fail under the cubic pullback metric, and contributes only polynomially many separated points on every compact subset, hence zero upper-capacity entropy.

originality.rationale: The closest 2026 source proves the same noncompact Bowen-Walters upper bound under global uniform small-time control and publicly frames removal of that hypothesis as an unresolved issue.
